pr_title: Set `out` parameters to default instead of using SkipInit in Interop generators
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/98049

To align with `DllImport` behavior, `out` parameters for `LibraryImport` and `GeneratedComInterface` should be default-initialized, never `SkipInit`'ed

issue_context.title: [API Proposal]: DefaultInitializeAttribute for out parameters in native marshallers
issue_context.body:
### Background and motivation

If you have an existing P/Invoke that has an `out` parameter, that parameter is still zero initialized unless you have the calling method declared as `SkipLocalsInit`. Translating a P/Invoke like this to a `DllImport` results in a behavior change, as the generated method has `SkipLocalsInit`, and doesn't initialize the local passed by pointer into the backing P/Invoke. So if your API previously was depending on the `out` value being zeroed upon entry, this is problematic. 

One of the bigger cases this is important, is if you're outting a custom struct with a custom marshaller. Many native methods will do error checking first, and not fill `out` variables on error. However, the custom marshaller does not know that the function errored, so it unconditionally will attempt to unmarshal the native value. Most unmarshallers could handle a zeroed struct, but would blow up with a garbage struct (Structs containing strings or arrays are the big offenders here). 

To solve this, add an attribute that can be applied to `out` variables that will default initialize the value for that out passed into native code. 

### API Proposal

```csharp
namespace System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshalling;

[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Parameter)]
public sealed class DefaultInitializeAttribute : Attribute
{
}
```


### API Usage

```csharp
    [LibraryImport("mylib", EntryPoint = "Function")]
    [UnmanagedCallConv(CallConvs = [typeof(CallConvCdecl)])]
    internal static partial void DoSomething([DefaultInitialize] out int status);
```


### Alternative Designs

Instead of `DefaultInitializeAttribute`, an alternative such as `AlwaysMarshalAttribute` could be used, where even for `out` variables the managed is marshalled into unmanaged. However, this breaks a fundamental contract of `out` variables, as the C# side would be reading from an `out` variable before setting it, rather than just zero initializing a variable passed down to native code.

### Risks

_No response_

This seems like general goodness, but I'd argue we should be initializing all `out` params regardless. I don't think there should be any need to make that request. It does impact performance to some degree, but I'd prefer correctness over performance for interop.
@jkoritzinsky or @jtschuster Any thoughts on making a quick fix for this or do you think the performance is important?

@AaronRobinsonMSFT One other note is https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/96886, where out variables are default initialized for stateful marshallers, but not for stateless marshallers or primitive values. So the existing behavior is already indeterminate.

> we should be initializing all `out` params regardless.

I agree, I've never been a big fan of using SkipLocalsInit, but I have no idea what the performance hit would be.

I'm inclined to agree. I'm not the biggest fan of SkipLocalsInit, especially on generated code where that might not be the expected behavior. I'd be inclined to make all `out` variables default initted, and then have an attribute that can be added onto those out parameter declarations to skip the init if its really important for performance.
`SkipLocalsInit` is important for good perf of stack allocated buffers. Try your micro-benchmark with a marshaller that needs one of those.

One thing to note is that you can still leave SkipLocalsInit. Just default init all variables that are passed down to native directly, without possible user intervention (I'm pretty sure this is exclusively `out` declared parameters). And then if a perf issue is found, an attribute could be added to skip assigning to default. But since out parameters can't be stack allocated buffers, the only case this is a performance issue is if a large struct is being passed `out`, which is fairly rare.

> Just default init all variables that are passed down to native directly

Yes. This is what we should do. I agree with @jkotas that removing `SkipLocalsInit` is too much. We do that because part of source generator policy is use stack allocated buffers which we guarantee by construction are properly initialized. The `out` parameter on the other hand isn't done that way and I think we should in this case because of interop and the lack of language enforcement. Anything else is purely a waste of CPU cycles.

> Am I testing the wrong stackalloc'ing marshallers?

Try to benchmark it with a single element array or a string that has just a single character.

> And then if a perf issue is found, an attribute could be added to skip assigning to default. 

I do not think that an attribute to control this behavior makes sense. It is too complicated.

If somebody runs into a perf issue with the source generated marshaling, they can write the marshaling by hand to workaround it.
